official.deadline_note: Masaryk University's host page still publishes an annual 15 March deadline, which is outdated; the awarding body's current call closes 15 April 2027 at 12:00 noon and that date governs. The online system opens only about 45 days before the deadline.
official.application_cycle: Call opens 1 January 2027 for the 2027/2028 academic year (stay starts September/October 2027 at the earliest)
official.status_note: The Fund's page states the Visegrad Scholarship Program 'Opens on Jan 1, 2027 at 12:00 PM'; final application deadline 15 April 2027 at 12:00 PM; results announced by 31 May 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official wording: 'Does the scholarship cover tuition fees? Not directly. Host institutions receive 2,000 EUR per semester per scholar. For master's studies, this covers tuition or administrative costs; excess fees are the scholar's responsibility. For post-master's, the lump sum covers institutional hosting expenses.'
benefits: EUR 3,500 per semester paid to each scholar's bank account - 'This money is at the scholar's full disposal'
EUR 2,000 per semester per scholar paid to the host institution
Scholarship paid in advance for each semester (5-month period) after the host university confirms arrival in writing
The Fund issues a scholarship confirmation which can be used as an enclosure to the visa application
eligibility: Open only to citizens of V4 countries (Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia) and of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, Northern Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine
The country of the applicant's citizenship must differ from the country of the host institution
Master's/post-master's scholarships require completed 6+ semesters or a bachelor's degree; Eastern Partnership and Western Balkans citizens can access only master's or post-master's programmes
Previous level of university studies must be completed in a country other than the one where the applicant applies
The distance between the applicant's current employer/university or permanent residence and the host institution should exceed 150 km
Support is for full-time Master's level studies or full-time post-Master's studies/research, 1-2 semesters
Preference is given to applicants not supported previously and to applicants with study/research topics relevant to the V4 region
requirements: Application form must be filled out in English
Each scholar can submit only one application to one host institution and for one study programme/research project per deadline
Applicants must disclose any concurrent scholarships; the Fund may withdraw its offer
The scholarship is an attendance scholarship - the scholar is expected to work on the study/research project at the host institution for the entire period
Recipients must acknowledge the Fund's support in scholarly documentation and public events and use the Visegrad Scholarship Program logo
Master's scholars need transcripts with 30+ ECTS credits and host enrolment confirmation for further installments; post-master's scholars must submit supervisor-signed progress reports
documents: Scanned valid ID document or passport
Master's level: scanned transcript of records covering at least the last two completed semesters, or a diploma supplement
Master's level: scanned letter of acceptance from the host university, or proof of application if not yet accepted when applying
Post-master's level: scanned letter of acceptance with a detailed working plan
Documents must be written in English or accompanied by a translation certified by a sworn translator or a university official
selection_criteria: Preference is given to applicants not supported previously by the Fund
Preference is given to applicants with study/research topics relevant to the V4 region
coverage: EUR 3,500 per semester stipend paid to the scholar
EUR 2,000 per semester per scholar paid to the host institution - for master's studies this covers tuition or administrative costs, for post-master's studies institutional hosting expenses
Excess tuition fees are the scholar's responsibility
Not covered: visa, insurance, accommodation and travel - 'the Fund cannot cover any additional costs'
application_method: Apply online via My Visegrad (my.visegradfund.org); the system opens approximately 45 days before the deadline
Upload all documents in the online system by 15 April 2027, 12:00 PM (noon); PDF format recommended
No documents or hard copies are sent by post
Results are notified by e-mail and published 45 working days after the submission deadline at the latest (announced by 31 May 2027)
The contract is mailed to the scholar's address after final acceptance; funds are released after the host confirms arrival
official.application_route: Apply online via My Visegrad (my.visegradfund.org) by 15 April 2027, 12:00 noon, with a host acceptance letter (or proof of application) obtained from the host faculty's international office.
official.citizenship_residency: Open only to citizens of V4 countries (Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia) and the Fund's listed Western Balkans and Eastern Partnership countries; the applicant's citizenship must differ from the host institution's country, and the distance from the applicant's current university/employer or permanent residence to the host must exceed 150 km.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - V4 citizens study in another V4 country or a listed WB/EaP country; citizens of the listed WB/EaP countries study in the Visegrad countries. Applicants may already be enrolled at the host university, but their previous degree must have been completed in another country.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All disciplines are eligible; the application form offers a choice of 25 disciplines. Preference is given to study/research topics relevant to the V4 region.
official.research_requirement: Post-master's applicants must submit a letter of acceptance with a detailed working plan approved by the host institution.
official.duration: 1-2 semesters (up to two semesters); the Fund pays each 5-month semester in advance
official.description: Visegrad scholarships support Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for up to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe.
official.region: Central and Eastern Europe (more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions)
official.program_type: Visegrad Scholarship Program - Master's and post-Master's study/research mobility scholarship of the International Visegrad Fund
official.english_requirement: No language certificates required and study may be in the native language of the university, but the application form must be filled out in English.

Whether the EUR 3,500/semester stipend meets living costs in Brno - the Fund publishes no guidance
verification.notes: Award amount (EUR 3,500/semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000/semester for the host institution), the 15 April 2027 noon deadline, conditions and required documents were taken from the International Visegrad Fund's official programme page; payment mechanics, tuition treatment, the English-language rule and the earliest start date were confirmed on the Fund's scholarships FAQ; host-side steps (letter of acceptance via the faculty international office) were confirmed on Masaryk University's CZS page, whose 15 March deadline and 1-4 semester wording are outdated.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a mobility stipend, not a full ride: the Fund pays you EUR 3,500 per semester and your host university EUR 2,000 per semester, so travel, visas, insurance, housing and any tuition above the host's lump sum remain yours to fund. Timing is unforgiving - although the call is announced on 1 January 2027, the My Visegrad system opens only about 45 days before the 15 April 2027 noon deadline, and nothing is accepted late. If Masaryk University is the target, approach the faculty international office months in advance for the letter of acceptance, remember selection is made by the Visegrad Fund, not by Masaryk, and check the 150 km rule before falling in love with Brno.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's or doctoral students from V4 or partner (Western Balkans/Eastern Partnership) countries who want one or two funded semesters of study or research at another institution in the region, away from their previous university.
application_readiness_checklist: Email the international office of your target Masaryk faculty (or other host) several months ahead to secure the letter of acceptance, or at minimum proof of application
Prepare a transcript covering your last two completed semesters, or a diploma supplement, plus a valid passport/ID scan
For post-master's applications, agree a detailed working plan with your prospective supervisor in advance
Verify you completed your previous degree in a country other than Czechia and that Brno lies more than 150 km from your current university or permanent residence
Register on My Visegrad early and keep every upload in PDF format
Diarise 15 April 2027, 12:00 noon as the hard cut-off and aim to submit days earlier
common_rejection_risks: Missing the noon deadline - the system closes and no late applications are accepted at all
Applying to a host institution in your own citizenship country, or returning to the country where your previous degree was completed
Arriving at the deadline with neither an acceptance letter nor proof of application
Submitting more than one application, host or project in the same round
Living or studying within 150 km of the host institution
Failing to disclose a concurrent scholarship such as Erasmus+, which can lead to the Fund withdrawing its offer
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to and from the host city, visa/residence-permit fees, health insurance, accommodation (Masaryk dormitory or private rent), any tuition or administrative fees above the EUR 2,000/semester institutional payment, and living costs beyond the EUR 3,500/semester stipend.
document_audit: The transcript must cover at least the last two completed semesters; a diploma supplement is accepted in its place
Any document not in English needs a sworn-translator or university-official certified translation
Only the post-master's track requires the detailed working plan; master's applicants need the acceptance letter or proof of application
Nothing is posted - every document is uploaded to My Visegrad before the deadline
If you applied with proof of application, the final acceptance letter is only required before the contract is signed
alerts: Masaryk University's page still advertises a 15 March deadline and stays of one to four semesters; the Fund's current cycle runs 1 January to 15 April 2027 with a maximum of two semesters - trust visegradfund.org over the host page
The call is announced on 1 January but the application system only opens roughly 45 days before the deadline, so early January gives you time to prepare, not to submit
With results out at the end of May, the stay can start no earlier than September/October of the same year
It is an attendance scholarship: you must be physically present at the host institution for the whole period
The first installment is released only after the host university sends written arrival confirmation; later installments require transcripts with 30+ ECTS or supervisor-signed progress reports
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Everything is filed electronically in My Visegrad before 15 April 2027, 12:00 noon; results follow by e-mail and website by 31 May 2027, then a posted contract, the host's arrival confirmation releases the funds, and the stay begins in September/October.
